wikifarm-mainpage-content-galaxy-userman: Illustration of an open book with a checkmark
Learn more about editing and organizing your content.
wikifarm-mainpage-content-galaxy-adminma: Illustration of a closed book with a cogwheel and a lock symbol
Get ready to manage an individual wiki or the entire Galaxy environment.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-i:
BlueSpice Galaxy is more than a classic wiki — it's a collection of different content types, each built for a specific kind of work. This page gives you a first idea what types of pages you can create.

You don't need any technical background to contribute your knowledge to your shared wiki(s). If you can write text and click a few buttons, you're ready.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-w: write a general article, guide, or informal page

This is the basic page type — the same kind of page you may know from Wikipedia. It usually lives in the main namespace and is the right choice for most everyday content: how-to guides, references, and general documentation.
Anytime you don't need approval workflows, version control, or a special layout. If in doubt, start here.

# Click the +-button in the header bar. # Enter a page name. # If your wiki offers a page template, select one. If not, your page will open directly in edit mode. # Use the editor toolbar to add text, headings, images, and links. # Save the page. You have just added a new page!
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-c: create a document that needs approval and structured data for document control
The Controlled documents namespace is there for content that needs to be official, reviewed, and traceable — for example: policies, procedures (SOPs), quality manuals, and so on.

Any content where you need proof of who approved what, and when — and where uncontrolled changes should never quietly become "official."

This means a document has a clear distinction between a "draft" version and the currently valid, officially released version. The document also shows other important information such as ownership and next review date.

# Click on '''Controlled documents''' in the main navigation.
# Enter a page name in the field '''Create Controlled document'''.
# Save the page.

You will notice a sidebox to enter the information about the document owner and other information to keep the document up-to-date. The document is now in draft status and needs to be approved before being officially valid.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-m: The '''Minutes''' namespace is built specifically for documenting meetings. When you create a new minutes page, it opens with a ready-made dashboard that helps you find and organize past meetings.

Any recurring or one-off meeting where you want notes that are easy to find later and consistent in structure.

* New minutes automatically use a page template, so you get a consistent structure (agenda, attendees, decisions, action items) every time — you just fill it in.
* Minutes are organized as '''subpages''', e.g. grouped by team, project, or recurring meeting series, so related meetings stay together and are easy to browse.

# Click on "'''Minutes'''" in the main navigation.
# Enter a page name in the field "'''Create Minutes'''".
# Save the page.

You can now prepare your meeting agenda and additionally add the invited and actual attendees in the infobox (the page's main Subject).
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-p: document a step-by-step business process or workflow

The '''Process''' namespace contains BPMN diagrams (based on a standard called ''Business Process Model Notation''). Each diagram can additionally produce wiki pages for each process step. The visual process diagram can later be included in any wiki page.
When you need to document ''how something is done'' step by step — an approval flow, an onboarding process, an incident-handling procedure — in a visual, easy-to-follow format rather than plain text.

# Click the '''+'''-button next to the link "'''Processes'''" in the main navigation. # Enter a process name.
This opens a page with the process editor. # Add your process shapes to the page. # Save the page. Process diagrams have to be validated to produce correct syntax in the background. Read the documentation if the "'''Save'''"-button
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-s: work with tables, calculations, or lists of data
Spreadsheets bring familiar table and calculation functionality directly into Galaxy. The values from cells in a spreadsheet can then additionally be used as a value for a chart or KPI visual.

Whenever your content is primarily tabular data, needs basic formulas or calculations, or would simply be clearer as rows and columns rather than a basic wiki table.

Spreadsheet cell and cell range values can later be used as values for KPIs or charts.

# Click the '''+'''-button next to the link "'''Spreadsheets'''" in the main navigation. # Enter a spreadsheet name.
This opens a page with the spreadsheet editor. # Edit your spreadsheet. # Save the page.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-b: Blog entries are technically wiki pages, but living in the Blog namespace, they behave differently:

Announcements, project updates, team news — anything meant to be read chronologically as a stream of shorter posts rather than looked up as reference material.

* Each blog post is its own page.
* The root/main blog page automatically displays a special layout showing previews (teasers) of the latest blog entries — like a news feed — so readers can scan and click through to full posts.

# Click the '''+'''-button next to the link "'''Blogs'''" in the main navigation. # Enter a blog post title and select the "'''General blog'''" or your "'''User blog'''" as parent page.
You can edit the blog page like any other wiki page. # Save the page. The blog entry is now listed on the blog overview page.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-l:
First, upload your logo to the Shared resources wiki if you want to reuse it for multiple subwikis. # In the top bar, open the menu that lists all wikis. Search for the "Shared resources" wiki. # Click the drop-down arrow next to the +-button and select "New file." # Drop your logo in the "Upload file" dialog. # Upload the file. # Follow the link to the uploaded file. # Click on the preview image on the file description page. # Copy the path of the image from the image path in your browser's address bar. It starts with /-shared/img_auth.php:
Example: /-shared/img_auth.php/5/5a/my-logo.png Next, add the logo path to your main wiki or any subwiki: # Switch to the wiki where you want to use the logo. # Click the "{{Icon|bi bi-gear|||}} '''Wiki actions'''" button (gear symbol) in the top bar. # Select "Configuration" in the Administration group. # Type "logo" in the search box. # Paste the logo path from your clipboard into the field. # Save the changes. # Refresh the page (Ctrl+F5).
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-s:
Galaxy is a knowledge environment where people collaborate freely and efficiently. Each team or domain, such as Engineering, HR, Sales, or Quality Management, has its own wiki with its own editors and access rules. Teams can organize their knowledge around their own processes and vocabulary, which makes pages easier to write and easier to find for the people who use them most. # Click the "{{Icon|bi bi-gear|||}} '''Wiki actions'''" button (gear symbol) in the top bar. # Select "Farm instances" in the Administration group. This opens the Farm manager. # Click "Create a wiki". Select the type of wiki you want to create (empty or from existing). # Provide a short Site name.
This name will be part of the site URL (e.g., for the site name "Mysubwiki" the path would become https://mygalaxy.com/Mysubwiki) # If the path should be different than the site name, change the suggested path. # Open the advanced settings. # Select the wiki type that fits your situation. # '''Important!''' Select the correct content language. This will determine the default language of the user interface. # Select a wiki color. # Select "Featured wiki" if you want it to be displayed in the "Featured" section of the Wiki list menu.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-u:
To manually add users to the wiki:

# Click the "{{Icon|bi bi-gear|||}} '''Wiki actions'''" button (gear symbol) in the top bar.
# Select "Users" in the Administration group. This opens the User manager.
# Switch to the tab "Users".
# Click "Add".
# Provide the user info and save the user.

If your users are organized in teams, you can create groups and add users to groups. This makes it easy later to assign the same role(s) to the same group of users in any of your Galaxy wikis.

# Switch to the "Groups" tab of the User manager.
# Click "Create group".
# Add a group name and save the group.

You can now switch to the user tab and assign this group to any user via the "Edit user" action.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-a:
Next, determine who can either read, edit, or approve pages in the wikis.

# Click the "{{Icon|bi bi-gear|||}} '''Wiki actions'''" button (gear symbol) in the top bar.
# Select "Access management" in the Administration group.
# Review the General setting (is your wiki public, protected, or private)?
# Switch to the "Roles" tab.
# Click "Add role assignment".
# Select a group or user and assign their role for this wiki.
wikifarm-gettingstarted-content-galaxy-s: If your Galaxy is already connected to an authentication provider so that you don't have to create users directly in your main wiki, you still need to assign them their roles in each wiki (unless this is handled by a script). To do so, follow the steps under "Manage access" in the previous section.
